title: Locally constant maps on a connected space are constant
statement: Let $X$ be a nonempty connected topological space [def-weil-connected-scheme] and let $E$ be a set. A map $f:X\to E$ is locally constant when every point has an open neighbourhood on which $f$ is constant; equivalently, every fibre $f^{-1}(\{e\})$ is open. If $f$ is locally constant, then $f$ is constant: there is an $e\in E$ such that $f(x)=e$ for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5): a Zariski-locally-constant map from a connected nonempty space to a set is constant; the fibre argument is the definition of connectedness.
